newsitem.title: USA: Consumer group says P&G's olestra causes problems.
newsitem.headline: Consumer group says P&G's olestra causes problems.

text.p: A consumer watchdog group Wednesday took its campaign against Procter & Gamble Co.'s food additive olestra to Indianapolis, a test-market for the fat substitute that the group says sickens consumers.

Hard on the heels of the news conference by the anti-olestra consumer group, the Centre for Science in the Public Interest, Cincinnati-based Procter & Gamble told reporters its side of the story, arguing that olestra had undergone extensive laboratory testing and was found safe.

"Wherever they have been test-marketed, they have been a hit," P & G spokeswoman Sydney McHugh said of the various salty snack foods made with "Olean" that have been test-marketed in Indianapolis and Columbus, Ohio.
"CSPI is just wrong on this issue and what we're trying to do is seperate fact from fiction. Most consumers won't have any complications" from eating the snacks, she said.

But Michael Jacobson, executive director of CSPI, said the group's Indianapolis hotline had been flooded with calls from hundreds of people who reported cramps, diarrhoea, fecal incontinence and other problems caused by eating the snacks.
"In just the first two weeks on the market, 'Wow' (brand) chips have probably sickened thousands of people," Jacobson said.
"The flood of calls we have received represents the tip of the iceberg. People have missed work or school, called their doctor, or didn't get to the bathroom on time."
